title: the DSG movement chapter part I - the check frames, swimming, breath, moving water, climbing, rappelling, jumping and the rope system
audit_comment: The DSG movement chapter part I pins the check frames (the 1d20 ability check equal-or-less with the dice substitution, the proficiency check strictly less), the swimming block (the proficiency gate with the 1/3 humanoid-monster chance, the three functions, Table 1 with the five encumbrance rows x the four functions in numerator/denominator cells, the levels+con endurance with the treading double and the 1/10 high-speed cut and the equal high-speed rest, the 4/3-inch base rates with the strength damage-bonus speed addendum capped at +3, the 20-foot dive with the 10-foot jump-in bonus and the 5-per-10 height ladder capped at the 40-foot jump, the 20-foot surfacing with the 5-foot passive-float slowdown and the armor-removal rounds), the breath economy (the 1/3 con base rounded up, the cumulative halvings, the one-round floor, the -2 cumulative con checks, the +1 nonswimming round), the moving-water effects (the relative-speed rule with the 40-foot stream example, the waterfall half damage with the breath save and the 100-foot/1-10 plunge split, the 1-10 danger rating as the check cadence with the 1d6 failed-check damage and the five-or-less high-speed forcing), the climbing block (the surface taxonomy, Table 2 with the nine rows and the thief-only rates halved for others with the dexterity adjustment, the 2x and 10x slippery fall multipliers, the 40 percent non-thief rating, the armor/race/surface modifier ladders, the tools with the 1d4 spike rounds and the 10 percent arrest failure and the 15 percent ice-slip, Table 3, the grapple throw at 1/3 strength x 10 with the noise ladder, the rappel at +50/+30 and 120 feet per round), the jumping block (the 20-foot head start, the one-segment jumps, Table 4 with the seven bands, the encumbrance and race modifiers with the 2-foot floor), and the rope system (the 50 percent protrusion chance, Table 5, the thrown loop with Table 6 and the 20 percent +1 percent ladder, the +30 crossing check each round, the swing with the -5 per 10 feet and the 1d6 per 20-foot section, the belay with the second check and the 3-foot edge rule and the -10 per faller, the roping-together cascade at -10) (rules/dsgmove.h, prefix dmv); census 428 -> 429.

consts.name: dmvPart1Lo
consts.comment: the movement chapter part I spans printed pp. 12-19: the swimming, breath, moving water, climbing, jumping and rope halves, through roping together.

consts.name: dmvPart1Hi
consts.comment: the part I chapter matter ends at printed p. 19; bridges, the expanded falling rules, spelunking, excavation, fatigue, darkness and slippery surfaces ride the next round.

consts.name: dmvPart1PdfLo
consts.comment: the part I pdf pages start at 13 (the offset: pdf = printed + 1, pinned at R503).

consts.name: dmvPart1PdfHi
consts.comment: the part I pdf pages end at 20.

consts.name: dmvCheckDie
consts.comment: an ability check is rolled on 1d20.

consts.name: dmvMonsterSwimNum
consts.comment: for humanoid monsters, assume a 1/3 chance that the creatures are able to swim (the numerator).

consts.name: dmvMonsterSwimDen
consts.comment: the denominator of the humanoid-monster swimming chance: 1/3.

consts.name: dmvSwimFuncCount
consts.comment: the swimming ability is divided into three functions: endurance (how long), speed (how fast) and diving (how deep in a single round).

consts.name: dmvUnderwaterRateNum
consts.comment: a character swimming completely underwater has his speed reduced to 2/3 of the maximum (the numerator).

consts.name: dmvUnderwaterRateDen
consts.comment: the denominator of the underwater speed cut: 2/3 of the maximum.

consts.name: dmvT1RowCount
consts.comment: Table 1 has five encumbrance rows: unencumbered, normal gear, heavy gear, very heavy gear and encumbered.

consts.name: dmvEndurExampleTurns
consts.comment: the printed example: a fighter/magic-user of levels 6/5 with a CON score of 12 could swim 23 turns when carrying normal gear.

consts.name: dmvEndurExampleUnencTurns
consts.comment: completely unencumbered the same character could swim for 46 turns - the Table 1 doubled endurance.

consts.name: dmvHighSpeedEndDiv
consts.comment: the endurance of a character swimming at high speed is reduced to 1/10 of its original value.

consts.name: dmvHumanSwimIn
consts.comment: the speed with which a character can swim begins at a base 4 inches per round for humans.

consts.name: dmvDemiSwimIn
consts.comment: the base swimming speed is 3 inches per round for demihumans and humanoids.

consts.name: dmvStrSpeedBonusMaxIn
consts.comment: the strength bonus added to swimming speed can never exceed +3 inches, even if the character damage bonus is greater.

consts.name: dmvStrExBonusIn
consts.comment: the printed example: a human character with a strength of 16 has a damage bonus of +1.

consts.name: dmvStrExSpeedIn
consts.comment: the strength-16 human could thus swim at 5 inches per round.

consts.name: dmvDiveRateFt
consts.comment: a character can normally swim downward 20 feet in a game round.

consts.name: dmvJumpDiveBonusFt
consts.comment: a character jumping or diving into the water from a place within a few feet of the surface can add 10 feet to the depth achieved on the first round.

consts.name: dmvPerHeightFt
consts.comment: for each 10 feet of height above the water surface, an additional depth can be added.

consts.name: dmvHeightDepthBonusFt
consts.comment: the additional depth per 10 feet of height: 5 feet.

consts.name: dmvMaxJumpHeightFt
consts.comment: the height additions run to a maximum of a 40-foot-high jump.

consts.name: dmvExampleDiveNormalFt
consts.comment: the printed dive example: the normal-gear character achieves a depth of 30 feet after the first round - the 20-foot rate plus the 10-foot jump-in bonus.

consts.name: dmvExampleDiveHeavyFt
consts.comment: the heavy-gear character sinks 60 additional feet after the jump, depth 70 after the first round - pinned as printed; NOTE the example text says his encumbrance TRIPLES the diving rate while the Table 1 heavy row DOUBLES it (the table is the authority, the R501 precedent; the very heavy row is the triple).

consts.name: dmvSurfaceRateFt
consts.comment: the rate at which a character can surface from a dive is 20 feet per round with normal encumbrance.

consts.name: dmvPassiveFloatSlowerFt
consts.comment: a character who is simply floating upward (an unconscious character, for example) moves five feet per round slower.

consts.name: dmvBackpackRemoveRounds
consts.comment: it takes one round to remove a backpack under water.

consts.name: dmvArmorRemoveBase
consts.comment: subtract the armor class of the armor (not including magical bonuses or shield) from 10 to determine the rounds required to remove it under water.

consts.name: dmvArmorExampleRounds
consts.comment: the printed example: a sinking character in chain mail (AC 5) can remove the armor in five rounds.

consts.name: dmvBreathConDiv
consts.comment: a character who has taken a large breath of air and is not performing strenuous exercise can hold his breath for a number of rounds equal to 1/3 his constitution score, rounded up.

consts.name: dmvMinBreathRounds
consts.comment: a character is always able to hold his breath for at least one round.

consts.name: dmvBreathCheckStep
consts.comment: each round after his breath runs out the character makes a constitution check to stay alive: the first check has no modifiers, with a -2 cumulative modifier each round thereafter, until he leaves the water or fails a check and dies.

consts.name: dmvBreathExampleRounds
consts.comment: the printed example: a character with a 16 constitution can hold his breath underwater for six rounds; the 7th-round check is unmodified, the 8th at -2, the 9th at -4, the 10th at -6.

consts.name: dmvExampleStreamFt
consts.comment: the printed example: a stream flowing 40 feet per round will carry swimming characters along at that speed, plus or minus their swimming speeds.

consts.name: dmvUpstreamHoldIn
consts.comment: by swimming upstream at the normal human swimming speed of 4 inches per round, a character could manage to stay in the same position relative to the banks.

consts.name: dmvExampleWashdownFt
consts.comment: dwarves and halflings with normal swimming speeds of 3 inches per round will be washed downstream 10 feet in the sample stream, even spending the entire round swimming upstream.

consts.name: dmvWaterfallDamageDiv
consts.comment: a character carried over a waterfall receives half the normal amount of damage for the distance of the fall.

consts.name: dmvShortPlungeMaxFt
consts.comment: with a successful save vs. breath weapon: if the fall is 100 feet or less, the character receives no damage from the plunge.

consts.name: dmvLongPlungeDiv
consts.comment: if the drop is greater than 100 feet, the saved character only receives 1/10 the normal damage for such a fall.

consts.name: dmvDangerRatingLo
consts.comment: the DM rates the danger of a rapid, rock-filled stream with a number from one to 10, one being the most dangerous.

consts.name: dmvDangerRatingHi
consts.comment: the top of the danger rating range: 10.

consts.name: dmvRockDmgDie
consts.comment: whenever a character fails a swimming check in a dangerous stream, the pounding against the rocks causes 1d6 points of damage.

consts.name: dmvPoleDiaDiv
consts.comment: a pole diameter cannot be greater than 1/4 the height of the character attempting to climb it, unless the character uses a rope.

consts.name: dmvSlopeFallDiv
consts.comment: even if the save vs. petrification after a fall on a sloping wall is unsuccessful, the fall only inflicts half of the normal damage.

consts.name: dmvSlightFallMult
consts.comment: slightly slippery surfaces are wet or crumbly: the chance of a character falling from one is twice normal.

consts.name: dmvSlipFallMult
consts.comment: slippery surfaces (running water, slime or algae, frost, ice or grease): a thief character chance of falling on one is ten times his normal chance.

consts.name: dmvExThiefRoll
consts.comment: the printed example: a 3rd-level thief would make a normal climb walls roll at 87 percent.

consts.name: dmvExFailurePct
consts.comment: the 3rd-level thief normal chance of failure: 13 percent.

consts.name: dmvExSlightFailPct
consts.comment: on a slightly slippery surface the thief has a 26 percent chance of failure, needing a roll of 74 or less for success.

consts.name: dmvExSlipRoll10
consts.comment: on a slippery surface a thief of 10th level only succeeds on a 90 or less.

consts.name: dmvExNormalRoll10
consts.comment: the 10th-level thief normal success roll: 99 or less.

consts.name: dmvHeavyClimbDiv
consts.comment: characters with heavy gear or very heavy gear move at half the movement rates listed for climbing characters.

consts.name: dmvNonThiefRatingPct
consts.comment: non-thief characters have a base climbing rating of 40 percent and use the same procedure as thieves, but with a lesser chance of success.

consts.name: dmvClimbRowCount
consts.comment: Table 2 has nine surface rows: very smooth, smooth with cracks, rough, rough with ledges, ice wall, pole, tree with branches, sloping wall, and rope and wall.

consts.name: dmvArmorMidPct
consts.comment: characters in chain, splint, scale or banded armor can climb, but suffer a -15 percent penalty to their chance for success.

consts.name: dmvArmorLightPct
consts.comment: characters in studded leather or padded armor suffer a -5 percent to their chances.

consts.name: dmvDwarfPct
consts.comment: the race climbing modifier: dwarf -5 percent.

consts.name: dmvGnomePct
consts.comment: the race climbing modifier: gnome -10 percent.

consts.name: dmvHalflingPct
consts.comment: the race climbing modifier: halfling -5 percent.

consts.name: dmvHalforcPct
consts.comment: the race climbing modifier: half-orc +5 percent.

consts.name: dmvTreeModPct
consts.comment: the climbing surface bonus: tree with branches +40 percent.

consts.name: dmvSlopeModPct
consts.comment: the climbing surface bonus: sloping wall +25 percent.

consts.name: dmvPoleModPct
consts.comment: the climbing surface bonus: pole +20 percent.

consts.name: dmvRopeWallModPct
consts.comment: the climbing surface bonus: rope and wall +40 percent.

consts.name: dmvSpikeRoundsDie
consts.comment: a spike takes 1d4 rounds to hammer into a wall surface.

consts.name: dmvSpikeNoiseMi
consts.comment: the clanging of a hammered spike can be heard up to a mile away in windless conditions.

consts.name: dmvSpikeFailPct
consts.comment: whenever a spike is called upon to arrest a fall, there is a 10 percent chance per character supported that it will give way; if it comes free, the characters fall the full distance (or twice the distance to the next spike).

consts.name: dmvSpikeExamplePct
consts.comment: the printed example: two characters roped together and relying upon one spike to arrest their fall give the spike a 20 percent chance of popping free.

consts.name: dmvRopeFallDiv
consts.comment: any character whose fall is broken by a rope suffers only half the damage a fall of that distance would normally inflict.

consts.name: dmvIceSpikeFailPct
consts.comment: spikes placed in ice have a 15 percent chance of pulling free per character whose weight suddenly pulls against them.

consts.name: dmvGrappleStrDiv
consts.comment: a character can throw a grappling hook upward a distance equal to 1/3 of his strength score, rounded up, times 10.

consts.name: dmvGrappleMultFt
consts.comment: the strength-to-feet multiplier of the grappling hook throw: 1/3 strength times 10 feet.

consts.name: dmvGrappleExampleFt
consts.comment: the printed example: a character with a strength of 15 could throw the hook up to a height of 50 feet.

consts.name: dmvSwingThrowRadiusFt
consts.comment: with a radius of 10 feet from his body cleared of obstacles for swinging the hook in a circle before the cast.

consts.name: dmvSwingThrowMult
consts.comment: the character can throw the hook twice as far horizontally as he could otherwise.

consts.name: dmvRecoilDie
consts.comment: if a grappling hook cast is unsuccessful, it takes another 1d4 rounds to coil the rope and prepare the hook for another throw.

consts.name: dmvSelfHitLoPct
consts.comment: if a character is directly underneath his target and the dice roll on the throw is 01-05.

consts.name: dmvSelfHitHiPct
consts.comment: the top of the self-hit throw range: 01-05.

consts.name: dmvSelfHitDie
consts.comment: the thrower is struck by the hook as it falls and suffers 1d6 of damage.

consts.name: dmvHookNoiseLoYd
consts.comment: a successful grappling hook throw is audible for 100-400 yards in ideal conditions.

consts.name: dmvHookNoiseHiYd
consts.comment: the top of the successful-throw noise range: 400 yards.

consts.name: dmvHookFailNoiseLoYd
consts.comment: an unsuccessful throw will raise a clang audible 200-800 yards away.

consts.name: dmvHookFailNoiseHiYd
consts.comment: the top of the failed-throw noise range: 800 yards.

consts.name: dmvSlipFreeDie
consts.comment: a catch-and-slip grapple will slip free after 1d6 rounds of supporting a load; characters who pull on the rope for that many rounds are able to dislodge the hook, if they take the time to check.

consts.name: dmvGrappleTargetCount
consts.comment: Table 3 has two grapple target rows: rocky ledge and wooden wall.

consts.name: dmvRappelModPct
consts.comment: to rappel successfully, the character must make a successful climbing check with a +50 percent modifier.

consts.name: dmvFreeHangModPct
consts.comment: a rappel can be made down a free-hanging rope, where the character has no wall to brace against, but in this case the modifier is only +30 percent.

consts.name: dmvRappelRateFt
consts.comment: a character can rappel up to 120 feet per round.

consts.name: dmvRunHeadStartFt
consts.comment: a running broad jump requires a 20-foot head start.

consts.name: dmvJumpFloorFt
consts.comment: in no case can jumping modifiers shorten a jump to less than two feet.

consts.name: dmvHeavyJumpFt
consts.comment: characters carrying heavy gear subtract one foot from the distance of their jumps.

consts.name: dmvVeryHvyJumpFt
consts.comment: characters with very heavy gear subtract two feet from their jumping distance.

consts.name: dmvEncumbJumpFt
consts.comment: encumbered characters subtract four feet - the DSG allows the encumbered jump at a penalty where the WSG forbids severe jumps outright (a pinned cross-book divergence).

consts.name: dmvHalflingJumpFt
consts.comment: halflings must subtract one foot from their total jumping distance.

consts.name: dmvDwarfJumpFt
consts.comment: dwarves and gnomes must subtract two feet.

consts.name: dmvJumpBandCount
consts.comment: Table 4 has seven level bands: 1-6, 7-9, 10-12, 13-15, 16-18, 19-22 and 23+.

consts.name: dmvProtrusionBasePct
consts.comment: if a random determination is needed, there is a base chance of 50 percent that a given crossing has some sort of protrusion for a tossed grappling hook to catch on.

consts.name: dmvTieoffProtrusionPct
consts.comment: the other end of the crossing rope can be tied off to a handy protrusion (a 50 percent chance of finding one), tied to a spike hammered into the stone, or held by a character.

consts.name: dmvRopeCrossModPct
consts.comment: a character crossing on a rope line is allowed a +30 percent modifier to his climbing rating for the check each round he is suspended.

consts.name: dmvCaveTargetPct
consts.comment: a suitable thrown-loop target is uncommon in a dungeon, but in a cave there is a base 20 percent chance that an appropriate stalagmite is located in a convenient position.

consts.name: dmvLoopPrepRadiusFt
consts.comment: the maximum thrown-loop range assumes the character has a clear radius of 10 feet around him to prepare the throw.

consts.name: dmvLoopBaseHitPct
consts.comment: the basic chance to hit with a thrown loop is 20 percent at maximum range.

consts.name: dmvLoopBonusPerFt
consts.comment: the thrown-loop chance is modified by +1 percent for each foot under maximum range.

consts.name: dmvLoopExampleMaxFt
consts.comment: the printed example: the 7th-level character maximum range is 50 feet.

consts.name: dmvLoopExamplePct
consts.comment: throwing a loop over a stalagmite some 30 feet distant, the 7th-level character has a 40 percent chance of success (20 plus the 20 feet under maximum).

consts.name: dmvLoopCoilDie
consts.comment: if a thrown loop is unsuccessful, the coiling of the rope for a second attempt takes 1d6 rounds.

consts.name: dmvLoopBandCount
consts.comment: Table 6 has five level bands: 1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16 and 17+.

consts.name: dmvSwingCheckStepPct
consts.comment: the swing-into-obstacle climbing check is modified by a -5 percent per 10 feet of rope between the character and the point at which the rope is fastened.

consts.name: dmvSwingCheckPerFt
consts.comment: the rope-length step of the swing check: each 10 feet of rope costs 5 percent.

consts.name: dmvSwingSectionFt
consts.comment: a character smashed into an obstacle during a swing takes 1d6 points of damage per 20-foot section of rope between him and the attached rope end.

consts.name: dmvSwingDmgDie
consts.comment: the swing damage die: 1d6 per 20-foot section of rope.

consts.name: dmvBelayEdgeFt
consts.comment: the second belay check is required of belayers on a sheer surface of any kind, and also of characters on a level spot but within three feet of the edge of the sheer surface, when the fall pulls them in the direction of the drop-off.

consts.name: dmvBelayPerFallerPct
consts.comment: each additional falling character on the rope subtracts 10 from the climbing success chance of the character attempting to belay.

consts.name: dmvRopeSlackLoFt
consts.comment: roping together ties the characters to a rope with 20 or 30 feet of slack between them.

consts.name: dmvRopeSlackHiFt
consts.comment: the top of the roping slack range: 30 feet between characters.

consts.name: dmvCascadePct
consts.comment: when one character arrests the fall of two, the successful character must check again with a -10 modifier, and the character next to the second character to fall must make a climbing check to catch the two.

consts.name: dmvCrossTargetCount
consts.comment: Table 5 has three crossing target rows: bare stone walls or floor, cave formations, and ruined foundation.

bools.name: dmvAbilityCheckEqualOrLess
bools.comment: the ability check is successful if the roll is equal to or less than the ability in question.

bools.name: dmvSubstituteDiceOk
bools.comment: occasionally an ability check calls for a certain combination of dice, as in a 4d6 dexterity check; the listed dice are substituted for the d20, and the purpose is still to roll the attribute score or less.

bools.name: dmvProfCheckStrictlyLess
bools.comment: a proficiency check is rolled on 1d20 and compared to the character rating in the given proficiency: rolls LESS than the rating are successful - the strict inequality that distinguishes the proficiency check from the equal-or-less ability check.

bools.name: dmvNoMagicAssumed
bools.comment: all of these rules assume the character uses no magical assistance; the effects of such devices, when used, always take precedence over a character innate swimming abilities.

bools.name: dmvSwimProfRequiredAfloat
bools.comment: characters without swimming proficiency are unable to remain afloat in water and drown in deep water unless they are aided.

bools.name: dmvBreathHeldWithoutProf
bools.comment: a character does not need swimming proficiency to be able to hold his breath.

bools.name: dmvAnimalsSwimIfForced
bools.comment: almost all animals can swim, if forced to; wolves and other canines willingly follow prey into water, while most felines swim only in desperation.

bools.name: dmvFireStoneNeverEnter
bools.comment: certain creatures - fire- and stone-based monsters in particular - never enter the water.

bools.name: dmvEnduranceNeedsBreath
bools.comment: endurance reflects how long a character can continue swimming without resting, and assumes that he can breathe while swimming, i.e. is not swimming through a completely water-filled passage.

bools.name: dmvEncCategoriesMatchPhb
bools.comment: the encumbrance categories match those described in the players handbook, page 101.

bools.name: dmvEncumberedSinks
bools.comment: an encumbered character cannot move through the water under his own power; if he enters the water, he will sink (the Table 1 footnote).

bools.name: dmvEnduranceLevelsPlusCon
bools.comment: a character swimming endurance is calculated by adding his total experience levels to his constitution score - the number of turns he can swim without rest.

bools.name: dmvTreadingDoublesEndurance
bools.comment: a character who is only attempting to stay afloat by treading water doubles the number of turns of his swimming endurance.

bools.name: dmvEndurOutMeansDrown
bools.comment: when a character runs out of endurance he will drown unless he can get out of deep water or find some means of staying afloat.

bools.name: dmvHighSpeedDoublesRate
bools.comment: a character can elect to swim at high speed, doubling his rate of movement with the endurance penalty.

bools.name: dmvHighSpeedRestEqual
bools.comment: immediately upon exiting the water, the high-speed swimmer must spend as much time resting as he spent swimming at high speed.

bools.name: dmvStrBonusIsDamageBonus
bools.comment: the strength bonus added to swimming speed is the strength DAMAGE bonus (the strength-16 +1 example swims at 5 inches) - the DSG keys the speed bonus on the damage bonus where the WSG keyed it on strength bands; a pinned cross-book divergence, both cap at +3.

bools.name: dmvDiveModifiedByEnc
bools.comment: the depth attainable on a diving round can be modified by encumbrance, as explained on Table 1.

bools.name: dmvJumpBonusUnmodifiedByEnc
bools.comment: the additions for diving into water are not modified by encumbrance: a character jumping into the water can dive an extra 10 feet regardless of whether he is completely unencumbered or carrying heavy gear.

bools.name: dmvSurfaceModifiedByEnc
bools.comment: the surfacing rate is modified by unusual encumbrance as shown on Table 1, and assumes the character is actively working to return to the surface.

bools.name: dmvHeavyMustActivelySwim
bools.comment: a character encumbered with heavy gear or greater must actively swim for the surface, or he does not rise at all.

bools.name: dmvIntentionalLoadingDmJudged
bools.comment: a character can intentionally load himself down (with rocks, etc.) to aid a dive and release the added weight when he wants to surface; the DM must decide how heavily the character must load himself to reach a certain encumbrance category.

bools.name: dmvBreathRoundedUp
bools.comment: the breath durations and their halvings are all rounded up: the 1/3 constitution base, the strenuous halving and the no-breath halving.

bools.name: dmvFullyEncumBreathBarred
bools.comment: a character cannot be fully encumbered while performing the nonstrenuous breath-holding functions (normal movement, searching for secret doors, picking a lock).

bools.name: dmvStrenuousHalvesBreath
bools.comment: strenuous exercise (fighting, subduing, lifting or moving a heavy weight, moving at high speed) cuts the underwater time in half, rounded up - cumulative with the no-breath halving.

bools.name: dmvFullyEncumAlwaysStrenuous
bools.comment: fully encumbered characters underwater are always considered to be performing strenuous exercise.

bools.name: dmvNoDeepBreathHalves
bools.comment: a character without a chance to take a deep breath before submerging has his underwater time halved (rounded up), cumulative with the strenuous halving.

bools.name: dmvConCheckAfterBreath
bools.comment: a character does not immediately die when his breath runs out: each round after, he makes the constitution check to stay alive with the -2 cumulative step.

bools.name: dmvNonswimBreathPlusOne
bools.comment: holding breath in nonswimming situations (to avoid breathing the surrounding air) uses the swimming formula but adds one round.

bools.name: dmvCantAvoidUnsuspectedGas
bools.comment: characters cannot use breath-holding to avoid the effects of a gas unless they suspect that a gas is about to be released.

bools.name: dmvSpeedRelativeToWater
bools.comment: a character swimming speed is relative to the water he occupies: the stream carries him along at its speed plus or minus his swimming speed.

bools.name: dmvRapidTransportUntilImpact
bools.comment: extremely rapid streams can move characters with enough momentum to do them considerable harm; until the character hits something, the water might prove a fast and direct form of transportation - submerged rocks and subterranean waterfalls change that impression quickly.

bools.name: dmvWaterfallSaveVsBreath
bools.comment: a character carried over a waterfall receives half the normal damage for the distance of the fall, except that a saving throw vs. breath weapon is allowed, with the avoid-the-obstacles results.

bools.name: dmvDangerRatingIsCadence
bools.comment: the stream danger rating tells how often a character must make a swimming proficiency check: the time between checks in rounds equals the rating - a stream rated one requires a check every round, one rated four every four rounds.

bools.name: dmvLowRatingForcesHighSpeed
bools.comment: in a stream rated five or less, characters must swim at high speed.

bools.name: dmvAllClassesLimitedClimb
bools.comment: members of all character classes have a limited ability to move up and down steep slopes, provided hand and footholds are available.

bools.name: dmvOnlyThievesSheer
bools.comment: only thieves have the capability to ascend sheer walls, cliffs and the like.

bools.name: dmvNonThiefRoughRoutes
bools.comment: other characters may try to climb very rough stone surfaces, as well as trees, poles, ropes and other simple routes.

bools.name: dmvMountaineerBoosts
bools.comment: the mountaineering proficiency can increase climbing abilities for both thieves and non-thieves.

bools.name: dmvThiefOnlySmoothTypes
bools.comment: walls that are very smooth, smooth with cracks, or rough can only be climbed by thieves, unless characters are using ropes, spikes or other tools.

bools.name: dmvIceNeedsTools
bools.comment: ice walls can only be climbed by characters (including thieves) using tools.

bools.name: dmvThiefOnlyRates
bools.comment: in all instances the Table 2 rates are for thieves only; all other characters move at half the thief rates.

bools.name: dmvDexAdjAddsToRate
bools.comment: all characters can add their dexterity reaction/attacking adjustments to their rate of climbing.

bools.name: dmvBarkNonslippery
bools.comment: any pole with tree bark still attached is considered a nonslippery surface.

bools.name: dmvRopeOnlyUnbracedCat
bools.comment: a rope only falls into the pole category if the character cannot brace his feet against a wall or some other surface to aid the climb.

bools.name: dmvSlopeSaveVsPetr
bools.comment: if a character falls while on a sloping wall surface, he can make a saving throw vs. petrification; if the save is successful, he takes no damage from the fall.

bools.name: dmvNonslipperyDrySolid
bools.comment: nonslippery surfaces are dry and solid; they do not crumble when touched, and a character chance of falling is calculated at the normal rate.

bools.name: dmvEncumbNoSheerWithoutTools
bools.comment: encumbered characters cannot climb sheer surfaces without the aid of tools.

bools.name: dmvHeavyGearHalfRate
bools.comment: the heavy-gear and very-heavy-gear climbing halving is cumulative with all other effects.

bools.name: dmvNormalGearFullRate
bools.comment: characters with no gear or normal gear can utilize the full climbing movement rates.

bools.name: dmvNonThiefCheckEqualOrLess
bools.comment: the non-thief climbing check is rolled on 1d100 against the modified climbing rating: a result greater than the rating indicates failure, a result less than or equal to the rating means success.

bools.name: dmvFailMeansNeverClimb
bools.comment: if a climbing check fails, the character can never climb that wall.

bools.name: dmvFailCostsOneRound
bools.comment: even a failed climbing attempt requires one round of game time.

bools.name: dmvNoPlateNoShield
bools.comment: characters cannot climb in any type of plate mail armor, nor can a shield be held by a climbing character.

bools.name: dmvLeatherNoPenalty
bools.comment: leather armor does not penalize a climber.

bools.name: dmvShieldSlungNoBenefit
bools.comment: a character can sling a shield over his shoulder to carry it along while climbing, but cannot receive any defensive benefit for a shield thus carried.

bools.name: dmvSpikeShortensFall
bools.comment: the usual function of a spike is to shorten the distance a character falls: a spike 200 feet up a cliff with 50 feet of slack in the rope turns a fall beginning 50 feet higher into a 100-foot fall (50 down to the spike, 50 more of slack).

bools.name: dmvUseMultipleSpikes
bools.comment: characters can help prevent spike-arrest accidents by using more than one spike.

bools.name: dmvIceSpikeEachRound
bools.comment: climbing an ice wall absolutely requires spikes: a spike must be driven into the ice wall before a character can climb, the process must be repeated each round, and since it takes a round to drive a spike, the process is doubly slow.

bools.name: dmvPoleWrapTechnique
bools.comment: a rope wrapped around a too-wide pole and pulled against as he climbs lets a character climb a pole whose diameter equals his own height; any pole wider than this should be treated as a wall.

bools.name: dmvRappelFailFallsFull
bools.comment: a failed rappel climbing check means a fall from the top to the bottom of whatever distance is involved.

bools.name: dmvRappelNormalRestrictions
bools.comment: all normal climbing restrictions (encumbrance, armor, etc.) apply to rappelling.

bools.name: dmvAllClassesJump
bools.comment: characters of all classes have a limited ability to jump across obstacles, the same procedure as given for acrobats (unearthed arcana page 24).

bools.name: dmvJumpOneSegment
bools.comment: all jumps require only one segment of time.

bools.name: dmvNoBackwardOrExtended
bools.comment: unlike acrobats, other characters cannot attempt to jump backward or leap in an extended position.

bools.name: dmvJumpNoNormalPenalty
bools.comment: unencumbered characters and characters carrying normal gear have no penalties to their jumping abilities - the encumbrance ladder starts at heavy gear.

bools.name: dmvJumpNoRacialHumans
bools.comment: humans, elves and half-orcs suffer no racial penalty on a jump.

bools.name: dmvFarSideAnchorProblem
bools.comment: the perennial rope problem is how to attach the rope to the far side: grapple-catchable irregularities are uncommon in a dungeon setting, more common in natural caves, and a once-bridged crossing invariably has wreckage of the bridge foundation to catch with a grappling hook.

bools.name: dmvArrowRopeImpractical
bools.comment: the rope-tied-to-the-arrow trick is dashing and romantic but impractical: an arrow trailing a rope and fired into wood is simply not strong enough to support even the lightest of characters.

bools.name: dmvRopeCrossCheckEachRound
bools.comment: a character crossing on such a line is in a precarious position indeed, and must make a climbing check each round that he is suspended.

bools.name: dmvRopeCrossModsApply
bools.comment: on a rope crossing the modifiers for armor and encumbrance still apply to the climbing check.

bools.name: dmvRopeAlwaysNonslippery
bools.comment: a rope is always considered a nonslippery surface.

bools.name: dmvRopeWallRateApplies
bools.comment: the rate of climb listed for rope and wall applies to characters making a crossing on a rope.

bools.name: dmvLoopThiefOrFamiliar
bools.comment: a thrown loop is a tricky maneuver that can only be attempted by thieves or other characters with a long and intimate familiarity with ropes (characters raised on farms, or who served as sailors).

bools.name: dmvLoopRangeHalved
bools.comment: the thrown-loop range is halved if the character does not have the clear 10-foot radius around him to prepare the throw.

bools.name: dmvLoopAttemptOneRound
bools.comment: a loop attempt takes one round; characters may make as many attempts as they wish, and the method carries the additional advantage of being virtually soundless.

bools.name: dmvSwingPendulum
bools.comment: a rope supported at one end swings to a point where it is hanging straight down; a weight attached to the rope is carried past that point by momentum, creating the pendulum motion that gives characters problems when they ram into a solid object during their swing.

bools.name: dmvSwingCheckToHold
bools.comment: if a character is holding a rope that swings into an obstacle, he must make an immediate climbing check to see if he can hold on; an unsuccessful check means he has been knocked off the rope and has fallen.

bools.name: dmvSwingDropFractions
bools.comment: the swing damage drops all fractions: a character on a 15-foot rope receives no damage, and a character 35 feet down a rope suffers only 1d6 points of damage.

bools.name: dmvAnyoneCanBelay
bools.comment: any character can attempt to protect another character against a fall with a belay; the only tool required is a rope, although spikes can add to the security of a belay.

bools.name: dmvBelayRopeTied
bools.comment: the character to be protected must have a rope tied securely around him; the character performing the belay holds the other end of the rope, but does not tie it to himself.

bools.name: dmvBelayPaysOutSlack
bools.comment: the belayer pays out the rope slowly as the protected character moves farther away from him; if the protected character should fall, the belayer grabs the rope tightly and braces himself to try to catch the shock of the weight.

bools.name: dmvBelayCheckArrests
bools.comment: the belayer must roll a climbing check to arrest the fall: if successful, the rope is held and the other character can fall no farther than the length of the rope; if unsuccessful, the rope runs through the hands of the belayer too quickly and the fall proceeds normally.

bools.name: dmvBelaySecondCheck
bools.comment: a belayer who successfully holds the rope but occupies a dangerous or narrow spot must make a second climbing check to maintain his hold on whatever surface he is clinging to; if the second check is unsuccessful, the belayer joins his companion in the fall.

bools.name: dmvBelaySpikeAnchored
bools.comment: a belayer performing from a dangerous spot can use a spike to anchor himself: he performs the belay normally, and if he arrests the fall but fails his second check so that he is pulled into the fall, the spike should then catch both falling characters - with the standing 10 percent per supported character chance of pulling loose.

bools.name: dmvBelayBothEndsNoChecks
bools.comment: a belay can hold one end of a rope used for support, as in a chasm crossing: with a grappling hook fastening the far side and a belay established on the near side, characters cross as if the rope were attached at both ends, and the character holding the rope makes no checks.

bools.name: dmvRopedNoSingleFall
bools.comment: a party roped together insures that no single member will suffer a damaging fall; however, the group takes the risk of all members falling together.

bools.name: dmvRopedSlowestRate
bools.comment: characters who are roped together must move at the rate of the slowest member, with the order of characters on the rope noted.

bools.name: dmvRopedBothSidesCheck
bools.comment: if one roped character falls, the characters on each side of him must make climbing checks: if both checks are successful the fall is stopped immediately; if one character arrests the fall but the other fails, the -10 two-faller re-check follows.

bools.name: dmvRopedCascadeRecheck
bools.comment: each time the weight of a new character is added to those who have fallen, the characters who have not fallen but are adjacent to those falling must make climbing checks; this continues until a successful climbing check is made on each side of the falling characters, or until the entire party falls.

bools.name: dmvRopedEndSingleCheck
bools.comment: if a character or characters on the end of the rope fall, only the single character next to the falling character must make a check - it is more advantageous to have either the first or the last character fall, especially if the character next to him is a skilled climber.

chains.name: dmvJumpBand
chains.comment: the broad-jumping level band chain: levels 1-6 band 0, 7-9 band 1, 10-12 band 2, 13-15 band 3, 16-18 band 4, 19-22 band 5, and 23 or up band 6 (the tail) - the band indexes the Table 4 rows.

chains.name: dmvLoopBand
chains.comment: the thrown-loop level band chain: levels 1-4 band 0, 5-8 band 1, 9-12 band 2, 13-16 band 3, and 17 or up band 4 (the tail) - the band indexes the Table 6 range rows.

tables.name: Table 1: SWIMMING EFFECTS OF ENCUMBRANCE
col_comments: The numerator of the endurance multiplier by encumbrance row (0 = the printed none, impossible).
The denominator of the endurance multiplier: doubled, normal, halved, quartered, none.
The numerator of the speed multiplier by encumbrance row (0 = the printed none).
The denominator of the speed multiplier: doubled, normal, halved, quartered, none.
The numerator of the diving multiplier - the one function that survives every encumbrance: normal, normal, doubled, tripled, tripled.
The denominator of the diving multiplier (always 1).
The numerator of the surfacing multiplier by encumbrance row (0 = the printed none).
The denominator of the surfacing multiplier: doubled, normal, halved, quartered, none.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 1 grid: the five encumbrance rows (unencumbered, normal gear, heavy gear, very heavy gear, encumbered) x the four functions (endurance, speed, diving, surfacing), each cell split into the numerator and denominator of the multiplier - a 0 numerator is the printed none (impossible)

tables.name: Table 2: RATES OF CLIMBING
col_comments: The nonslippery climbing rate in feet per round by surface row: 6, 12, 18, 24, dash, 36, 60, 60, 40 (0 = the printed dash, thieves with tools only for ice).
The slightly slippery rate in feet per round by surface row: 3, 6, 9, 12, dash, 24, 40, 30, 30 (0 = the printed dash).
The slippery rate in feet per round by surface row: 0, 3, 6, 9, 6, 12, 20, 15, 20 (0 = the printed dash).
tables.audit_comment: the Table 2 grid: the nine surface rows (very smooth, smooth with cracks, rough, rough with ledges, ice wall, pole, tree with branches, sloping wall, rope and wall) x the three surface conditions (nonslippery, slightly slippery, slippery), in feet per round - a 0 cell is the printed dash (unclimbable: the very smooth slippery cell and both ice cells except slippery-with-tools)

tables.name: Table 3: GRAPPLING SUCCESS
col_comments: The miss maximum of the d100 grapple throw by target row: 01-88 miss on a rocky ledge, 01-70 on a wooden wall.
The catch-and-slip maximum by target row: 89-93 on a rocky ledge, 71-74 on a wooden wall.
The catch maximum by target row: 94-00 on a rocky ledge, 75-00 on a wooden wall.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 3 grid: the two grapple target rows (rocky ledge, wooden wall) x the three outcomes (miss, catch and slip, catch), each cell the d100 maximum of its range

tables.name: Table 4: BROAD JUMPING
col_comments: The standing broad jump die by level band (4 = 1d4, 6 = 1d6): 1d4 for the 1-6 and 7-9 bands, 1d6 for the 10-12 through 23+ bands.
The standing broad jump plus feet by level band: 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 - the 1d4+1 through 1d6+6 ladder.
The running broad jump die by level band (4 = 1d4, 6 = 1d6).
The running broad jump plus feet by level band: 5, 6, 5, 6, 9, 12, 15 - the 1d4+5 through 1d6+15 ladder.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 4 grid: the seven level bands (1-6, 7-9, 10-12, 13-15, 16-18, 19-22, 23+) x the standing and running broad jumps, each cell split into the die and the plus feet (non-acrobats)

tables.name: Table 5: CROSSING WITH A GRAPPLE
col_comments: The miss maximum of the d100 crossing throw by target row: 01-82 bare stone walls/floor, 01-75 cave formations, 01-66 ruined foundation.
The catch-and-slip maximum by target row: 83-89, 76-80, 67-71.
The catch maximum by target row: 90-00, 81-00, 72-00.
tables.audit_comment: the Table 5 grid: the three crossing target rows (bare stone walls/floor, cave formations, ruined foundation) x the three outcomes (miss, catch and slip, catch), each cell the d100 maximum of its range

tables.name: Table 6: THROWN LOOP RANGES
col_comments: The maximum thrown-loop range in feet by level band: 40, 50, 60, 75, 90 (non-acrobats).
tables.audit_comment: the Table 6 grid: the five level bands (1-4, 5-8, 9-12, 13-16, 17+) x the maximum thrown-loop range in feet - the 40 through 90 ladder
